reasons: Each rule has a matching test with a clear failure message.
The file states it does not prove a real cache hit, so that gap is known.

terms.meaning: a model provider feature that reuses the start of a prompt across calls, charging less for the reused part
the fixed opening text of every prompt in a run, placed before the per-process content
a short fingerprint of a piece of text, used to tell whether it changed
tidying text (spacing, line endings, character forms) so equal content always looks equal
a marker telling the model where the reusable part of the prompt ends

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: File setup and sample inputs
sections.what: Imports the prompt builder pieces, time types, and the evidence types. Defines sample industry text, sample taxonomy text, and two sample process identifiers. The docstring explains what the tests prove and what they cannot.
sections.why: The docstring says a cache miss causes no test failure, so these checks exist to catch it.
sections.watch_out: Passing these tests does not prove a live cache hit.

sections.name: pack
sections.title: Fake evidence pack builder
sections.what: Builds a sample evidence pack for a process, with one evidence item or none when empty is requested.
sections.why: Reason not stated beyond use as shared test input.

sections.name: TestPrefixIsStableAcrossProcesses
sections.title: Prefix stays identical across processes
sections.what: Checks repeated builds from the same industry and taxonomy text give identical text and digest. Checks the builder takes no process argument, and that no process or evidence identifier appears in the prefix.
sections.why: The docstring says the whole design depends on one shared prefix per run.
sections.watch_out: Any per-process text added to the prefix would break reuse without any error.

sections.name: TestPrefixCannotSeeAClock
sections.title: Prefix cannot read a clock
sections.what: Checks the prompt module does not import time, date, randomness or identifier-generating modules. Also checks the prefix contains no timestamp or bare date.
sections.why: The docstring says one current-time value in the prefix would change it on every call.
sections.watch_out: Adding a harmless time line to the prompt will fail the import check.

sections.name: TestNormalisationIsTheSingleChokepoint
sections.title: Text tidying for one prefix
sections.what: Checks the normalising step strips trailing spaces, collapses blank runs, leaves one final newline, unifies line endings, and applies Unicode composition. Also checks untidy inputs give the same prefix as tidy ones.
sections.why: The docstring says whitespace differences would create separate cache entries without any report.
sections.watch_out: Changing the normalising step changes every prefix digest at once.

sections.name: TestPrefixContent
sections.title: Prefix contents and order
sections.what: Checks the prefix contains the methodology, industry context and taxonomy in that order. Checks the methodology states its binding rules, and that a different industry gives a different digest.
sections.why: The docstring says the cache is per run, so the digest must differ between industries.
sections.watch_out: Reordering the sections changes the prefix and so the cache key.

sections.name: TestBreakpointPlacement
sections.title: Cache marker placement
sections.what: Checks the prefix carries one ephemeral cache marker. Checks per-process evidence and the task text sit in the message after the marker, not in the prefix.
sections.why: The docstring says per-process content must sit after the breakpoint.
sections.watch_out: Moving process text above the marker would prevent reuse across processes.

sections.name: TestEvidenceRendering
sections.title: Evidence rendering rules
sections.what: Checks an empty pack says retrieval returned nothing and that this is not an error. A populated pack lists citable identifiers. Undated items show as undated, and rendering is repeatable.
sections.why: Reason not stated beyond the test names.
sections.watch_out: Undated evidence must not receive an invented date.

sections.name: TestPromptVersioning
sections.title: Prompt versioning and immutability
sections.what: Checks the prefix digest changes when the prefix changes. Checks the prompt version is stable, ignores trailing whitespace, and changes with content. Checks the prefix object cannot be edited after creation, and its digest depends only on its text.
sections.why: Likely reason: the version and digest identify which prompt a run used.
sections.watch_out: A digest change means cache entries from earlier runs will no longer match.

summary: A set of tests that checks the shared part of every AI prompt is identical across processes in a run, so the model's cache can be reused and costs stay low.
purpose: Protects cost. A cache miss still gives correct output, but costs more, and nothing else would report it.
why: The module docstring says a cache miss fails nothing, so the test is the only check. It proves the prefix is stable, not that a real cache hit happens.
how: Pytest loads the file. Sample industry and taxonomy text are fed to the prefix builder. Tests compare repeated builds, search the prefix for process or evidence identifiers and timestamps, check the normalising step, check breakpoint placement, and check version digests.
inputs: Sample industry context text, sample taxonomy text, sample process identifiers, and fake evidence packs.
outputs: Pass or fail results for each test. Nothing is written to disk.
risks: The tests cannot prove an actual cache hit, which needs a live model call and a prefix long enough for the model to cache. Those checks live elsewhere.
debug: If a stability test fails, look for per-process text added to the prefix builder. If the digest test fails, check whether the methodology or taxonomy text changed. If the clock check fails, look for a new time import in the prompt module.
